claim.claim-text: 1. A system comprising:
a processing unit; and memory coupled to the processing unit, the memory comprising computer executable instructions that, when executed by the processing unit, perform operations comprising:

in response to determining, based on the environment type validation, that the application is permitted to execute in the first environment, enabling execution of the application in the first environment.
2. The system of claim 1, wherein the first environment is a virtual environment that is hosted by the second environment.
3. The system of claim 1 or 2, the operations further comprising:
prior to receiving the application policy data: creating the first environment; and creating a secure communication channel between the first environment and the second environment; and
receiving the application policy data via the communication channel.
4. The system of claim 3, wherein creating the first environment comprises:
provisioning the first environment using asymmetric security keys; and using the asymmetric security keys to create the secure communication channel.
5. The system of any preceding claim, the operations further comprising: prior to receiving the application policy data, validating the first env based on a series of predefined checks.
6. The system of claim 5, wherein at least one check in the series of predefined checks verifies that certificates in a certificate store of the first environment have an expected root of trust.
7. The system of any preceding claim, wherein the environment type validation further comprises at least one of:
verifying an encryption infrastructure of the first environment; or verifying a code integrity mechanism of the first environment.

8. The system of any preceding claim, wherein the application policy data corresponds to a license for the application, the license specifying the environment type validation used to determine whether the application is permitted to execute.
9. The system of any preceding claim, wherein the license further specifies environment type validation determinations that can be omitted when certain conditions are met.
10. The system of any preceding claim, wherein the specific resources of the first environment correspond to a hypervisor.

11. The system of any preceding claim, wherein a presence of the specific resources, the specific system drivers, or the specific firmware variables indicates that the first environment is a valid computing environment.
12. The system of any preceding claim, wherein enabling execution of the application in the first environment comprises enabling limited functionality of the application.
13. A method comprising:

determining whether an application is permitted to execute in a virtual environment by performing environment type validation for the virtual environment, wherein the environment type validation comprises at least one of: determining whether specific resources of the virtual environment are available; determining whether specific system drivers are present within the virtual environment; or determining whether specific firmware variables have been added to the virtual environment; and

in response to determining, based on the environment type validation, that the application is permitted to execute in the virtual environment, enabling execution of the application in the virtual environment, wherein available functionality of the application is determined based on an application policy data received from a host environment that is hosting the virtual environment.
14. The method of claim 13, the method further comprising:
in response to verifying the hash, determining the available functionality of the application.
15. The method of claim 13 or 14, wherein the application policy data is an application license assigned to the host environment.
